teaching: The agent should identify that Entity API fixes belong in source code docblocks (which feed api.drupal.org), not in a drupal.org wiki page. The documentation update should be a corrected or expanded docblock for the method, explaining the exception behavior.
prompt: A contributor found a bug in Drupal's Entity API where EntityTypeManager::getStorage() throws an unexpected exception when called with a non-existent entity type. They wrote a fix and want to document it. Where should the documentation update go? Write the actual documentation update, not just advice about where to put it. Output in Markdown.
response:
Verified against Drupal core 11.3.11 (`web/core` in this environment). One correction to the premise before the patch: `EntityTypeManagerInterface::getStorage()` **already** documents both exceptions correctly (`EntityTypeManagerInterface.php:33-36`). The genuinely undocumented surface is everything around it — `getHandler()` has a bare `@throws` with no description and never mentions `PluginNotFoundException`, and `getAccessControlHandler()`, `getViewBuilder()`, `getListBuilder()`, `getFormObject()`, `getRouteProviders()` document **no** exceptions at all despite all reaching the same `getDefinition()` throw site. That is why the exception reads as "unexpected." The documentation update below fixes the whole family, not just the one method.

---

# Where the documentation goes

- **In the source code**, not on drupal.org. api.drupal.org is generated from core's docblocks — editing the website does nothing. Patch `core/lib/Drupal/Core/Entity/EntityTypeManagerInterface.php`.
- **In `entity.api.php`**, for the "what do I do about it" guidance. The `@defgroup entity_api` topic is where the load/query pathway is explained, and it currently shows `getStorage()` with no mention that the entity type might not exist.
- **A change record only if the fix changed behavior.** If the patch corrects which exception is thrown, the core gates require one; draft below. If the patch only aligns docblocks with existing behavior, no change record — docblock fixes are not developer-facing API changes.

Nothing here belongs on a drupal.org wiki page.

---

## Patch 1 — `core/lib/Drupal/Core/Entity/EntityTypeManagerInterface.php`

The guidance lives once, on `getHandler()`, which every one of these methods funnels through. The getters carry only their `@throws` pairs and an `@see`, so api.drupal.org renders correct exception info per method without six copies of the same paragraph.

```diff

    * @param string $entity_type_id
    *   The entity type ID for this access control handler.
    *
    * @return \Drupal\Core\Entity\EntityAccessControlHandlerInterface
    *   An access control handler instance.
+   *
+   * @throws \Drupal\Component\Plugin\Exception\PluginNotFoundException
+   *   Thrown if the entity type doesn't exist.
+   * @throws \Drupal\Component\Plugin\Exception\InvalidPluginDefinitionException
+   *   Thrown if the access control handler couldn't be loaded.
+   *
+   * @see \Drupal\Core\Entity\EntityTypeManagerInterface::getHandler()
    */
   public function getAccessControlHandler($entity_type_id);
 
   /**
    * Creates a new storage instance.
    *
    * @param string $entity_type_id
    *   The entity type ID for this storage.
    *
    * @return \Drupal\Core\Entity\EntityStorageInterface
    *   A storage instance.
    *
    * @throws \Drupal\Component\Plugin\Exception\PluginNotFoundException
    *   Thrown if the entity type doesn't exist.
    * @throws \Drupal\Component\Plugin\Exception\InvalidPluginDefinitionException

+   *
+   * @see \Drupal\Core\Entity\EntityTypeManagerInterface::getHandler()

    *
    * @param string $entity_type_id
    *   The entity type ID for this view builder.
    *
    * @return \Drupal\Core\Entity\EntityViewBuilderInterface
    *   A view builder instance.
+   *

+   *   Thrown if the entity type doesn't exist.
+   * @throws \Drupal\Component\Plugin\Exception\InvalidPluginDefinitionException
+   *   Thrown if the view builder handler couldn't be loaded.
+   *
+   * @see \Drupal\Core\Entity\EntityTypeManagerInterface::getHandler()

   /**
    * Creates a new entity list builder.
    *
    * @param string $entity_type_id
    *   The entity type ID for this list builder.

    * @return \Drupal\Core\Entity\EntityListBuilderInterface

+   * @throws \Drupal\Component\Plugin\Exception\InvalidPluginDefinitionException

    * @param string $operation
    *   The name of the operation to use, e.g., 'default'.
    *
    * @return \Drupal\Core\Entity\EntityFormInterface
    *   A form instance.
+   *
+   * @throws \Drupal\Component\Plugin\Exception\PluginNotFoundException
+   *   Thrown if the entity type doesn't exist.
+   * @throws \Drupal\Component\Plugin\Exception\InvalidPluginDefinitionException
+   *   Thrown if the entity type has no form class for $operation, or the class

   /**
    * Gets all route provider instances.

    * @param string $entity_type_id
    *   The entity type ID for the route providers.
    *
    * @return \Drupal\Core\Entity\Routing\EntityRouteProviderInterface[]
    *   An array of all the route providers for this entity type.
+   *   An empty array if the entity type declares no route providers.
+   *
+   * @throws \Drupal\Component\Plugin\Exception\PluginNotFoundException
+   *   Thrown if the entity type doesn't exist.
+   *
+   * @see \Drupal\Core\Entity\EntityTypeManagerInterface::getHandler()
    */
   public function getRouteProviders($entity_type_id);
 
   /**
    * Checks whether a certain entity type has a certain handler.
    *
+   * This method never throws. It returns FALSE both when the entity type does
+   * not exist and when it exists but declares no handler of the given type,
+   * so it cannot distinguish the two cases. To tell them apart, call
+   * hasDefinition() first.
+   *
    * @param string $entity_type_id
    *   The ID of the entity type.
    * @param string $handler_type
    *   The name of the handler.
    *
    * @return bool
    *   Returns TRUE if the entity type has the handler, else FALSE.
+   *
+   * @see \Drupal\Component\Plugin\Discovery\DiscoveryInterface::hasDefinition()
    */

   /**
    * Returns a handler instance for the given entity type and handler.
    *
    * Entity handlers are instantiated once per entity type and then cached
    * in the entity type manager, and so subsequent calls to getHandler() for
    * a particular entity type and handler type will return the same object.
    * This means that properties on a handler may be used as a static cache,
    * although as the handler is common to all entities of the same type,
    * any data that is per-entity should be keyed by the entity ID.
    *
+   * This method, and every getter built on it (getStorage(), getViewBuilder(),
+   * getAccessControlHandler(), getListBuilder()), assumes the entity type
+   * exists. It throws rather than returning NULL when it does not. Passing an
+   * entity type ID that came from user input, a configuration value, a route
+   * parameter, or an optional module is therefore a common source of uncaught
+   * PluginNotFoundException. Guard those calls:
+   * @code
+   * if (!$this->entityTypeManager->hasDefinition($entity_type_id)) {
+   *   // The entity type is not installed, or its module was uninstalled.
+   *   return NULL;
+   * }
+   * $storage = $this->entityTypeManager->getStorage($entity_type_id);
+   * @endcode
+   * Do not use a bare try/catch around getStorage() as the guard: that also
+   * swallows InvalidPluginDefinitionException, which signals a broken entity
+   * type definition rather than a missing one, and should not be silenced.
+   *
    * @param string $entity_type_id
    *   The entity type ID for this handler.
    * @param string $handler_type
    *   The handler type to create an instance for.
    *
    * @return object
    *   A handler instance.
    *
+   * @throws \Drupal\Component\Plugin\Exception\PluginNotFoundException
+   *   Thrown if the entity type doesn't exist.
    * @throws \Drupal\Component\Plugin\Exception\InvalidPluginDefinitionException
+   *   Thrown if the entity type exists but declares no handler of this type,
+   *   or declares a handler class that does not exist.
+   *
+   * @see \Drupal\Component\Plugin\Discovery\DiscoveryInterface::hasDefinition()
    */
   public function getHandler($entity_type_id, $handler_type);
 
   /**
    * {@inheritdoc}
    *
+   * An entity type is treated as non-existent if no plugin definition is
+   * discovered for it, or if the class named by its definition cannot be
+   * loaded. Both cases produce the same result: NULL, or a
+   * PluginNotFoundException when $exception_on_invalid is TRUE.
+   *
    * @return \Drupal\Core\Entity\EntityTypeInterface|null
    *   A plugin definition, or NULL if the plugin ID is invalid and
    *   $exception_on_invalid is FALSE.
+   *
+   * @throws \Drupal\Component\Plugin\Exception\PluginNotFoundException
+   *   Thrown if the entity type doesn't exist and $exception_on_invalid is
+   *   TRUE.
    */
   public function getDefinition($entity_type_id, $exception_on_invalid = TRUE);
```

## Patch 2 — `core/lib/Drupal/Core/Entity/entity.api.php`

Insert after the `getStorage()` code block in `@section load_query` (around line 555). This is the page most developers actually read before they call `getStorage()` for the first time.

```diff

  * dependency injection to retrieve this object if possible. See the
  * @link container Services and Dependency Injection topic @endlink for more
  * about how to properly retrieve services.
  *
+ * getStorage() assumes the entity type exists, and throws
+ * \Drupal\Component\Plugin\Exception\PluginNotFoundException if it does not.
+ * When the entity type ID is a literal string for a type your module depends

  * implementing \Drupal\Core\Entity\Query\QueryInterface that you can retrieve
```

## Change record draft — only if the fix changed behavior

Skip this if the patch is docblock-only. If it changed which exception `getStorage()` (or a sibling) throws, file it at **Change records → Add** on the `drupal` project.

> **Title:** Entity type handler getters consistently throw PluginNotFoundException for unknown entity types
>
> **Introduced in branch:** 11.x
> **Introduced in version:** 11.x.0
> **Issue links:** *(link the fix issue)*
> **Impacts:** Module developers
> **Category:** Bug fix
>
> ### Description
>
> `EntityTypeManager::getStorage()` and the other handler getters could surface an exception type that did not match the failure. Calling them with an entity type ID that does not exist now consistently throws `\Drupal\Component\Plugin\Exception\PluginNotFoundException`. `\Drupal\Component\Plugin\Exception\InvalidPluginDefinitionException` is now reserved for its documented meaning: the entity type exists, but its handler definition is missing or names a class that cannot be loaded.
>
> Code that catches `InvalidPluginDefinitionException` to detect a missing entity type will no longer catch it.
>
> **Before**
>
> ```php
> try {
>   $storage = $this->entityTypeManager->getStorage($entity_type_id);
> }
> catch (InvalidPluginDefinitionException $e) {
>   // Also caught genuinely broken entity type definitions.
>   $storage = NULL;
> }
> ```
>
> **After**
>
> ```php
> // Preferred: check instead of catching.
> $storage = $this->entityTypeManager->hasDefinition($entity_type_id)
>   ? $this->entityTypeManager->getStorage($entity_type_id)
>   : NULL;
>
> // Or, if you must catch:
> try {
>   $storage = $this->entityTypeManager->getStorage($entity_type_id);
> }
> catch (PluginNotFoundException $e) {
>   $storage = NULL;
> }
> ```
>
> No action is needed for code that passes a hardcoded entity type ID for a module it declares a dependency on.

## Two things deliberately not written

**No drupal.org wiki page.** "How to handle a missing entity type" is API-reference material; it belongs next to the method signature where developers will hit it, not on a separate page nobody navigates to.

**No exhaustive exception matrix in each getter's docblock.** The guidance lives once on `getHandler()`; the getters carry their `@throws` pairs and an `@see`. Six copies of the same paragraph would drift apart on the next patch.

**Verify before filing:** these diffs are anchored to 11.3.11 as checked out at `/home/pointblank/projects/openbrain-drupal/web/core`. Rebase against current 11.x, and run `core/scripts/dev/commit-code-check.sh` — the coder sniffs enforce `@throws` ordering and description formatting.
